report.source_text: The neoplastic cells were weakly reactive for synaptophysin, and CD99 staining showed a membranous pattern (Fig. 6). In a subset, GATA-3 was positive and PAX-8 was weakly positive (Figs. 7 and 8). However, the neoplastic cells were nonreactive to ER (breast marker) and SATB2 (lower gastrointestinal and osteosarcoma marker). Moreover, the tumor cells were negative for Oscar pankeratin, CK7, CK20, Moc-31, TTF-1, WT-1, HMB45, Melan-A, SOX-10, S100, Inhibin, SMA, MyoD1, CD117, CD45, CD30, and CD34.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 37-year-old female presented with 4 months of dyspnea, back pain, and neck pain with tachypnea. Initial chest imaging showed right upper lobe consolidation and near-complete lobar collapse with enlarged lymph nodes. Initial transthoracic lung biopsy was non-diagnostic, showing fibrosis and lymphocytic infiltration without malignancy. Spine MRI detected a C7 compression fracture and lytic vertebral lesions consistent with metastatic disease. Subsequent fluoroscopy-guided liver biopsy revealed a malignant undifferentiated epithelioid neoplasm with hyalinized sclerotic stroma and weak neuroendocrine differentiation. Immunohistochemistry showed MUC4 positivity and a distinctive marker profile consistent with sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma. Next-generation genetic testing excluded known cancer risk gene mutations. Molecular testing specific for FUS gene rearrangement, ordered but not documented, was planned to confirm diagnosis. Overall, clinical, radiologic, histologic, and immunophenotypic evidence strongly supports the diagnosis of sclerosing epithelioid fibrosarcoma.
